sentences.text: Diplodoselache possessed a single dorsal fin with a spine similar to those found on the heads of other xenacanthiform fishes.
The largest complete Diplodoselache specimen measured 1.12 meters, though Dick suggested some individuals may have been considerably larger than one meter.
John Dick described the genus Diplodoselache in 1981 using four complete skeletons found in Viséan-stage ironstone concretions.
The type species Diplodoselache woodi honors Stan Wood, who found the first complete fossils in Scotland's Midland Valley region.
Diplodoselache was a predator that lived in lagoonal environments.
Diplodoselache is classified within the xenacanth family Diplodoselachidae.
Diplodoselache was an extinct cartilaginous fish that lived during the Carboniferous period in Scotland and possibly Russia.
Diplodoselache lived between 339.9 and 335.9 million years ago during the Visean stage.
